summary: Security remains strategically coherent and its codified top priorities still match the product stack, but the main gap remains unchanged: the OS↔PXS boundary is declared more strongly than it is enforced in runtime evidence, while tool/evidence hardening and reproducible posture-to-enforcement loops remain incomplete.

materialChanges.text: Security now has a canonical 08-research layer with domain map, radar, deep-dive index, doctrine, implications, and sources.
Security explicitly adopted an artifact-first research model with broad radar and bounded deep dives.
No material improvement yet in the top execution risk: OS↔PXS boundary enforcement remains the strongest live control gap.

topPriorities.title: Enforce the OS↔PXS boundary as a real control
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: The strongest current security risk remains cross-domain blast radius beyond the declared architecture boundary.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Product plan, risks, boundary artifact, deployment baseline, and Vega acceptance evidence all continue to point to boundary enforcement failure as the highest-risk live gap.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Close the current cross-domain read FAIL, align Vega/PX boundary enforcement to the declared model, and re-run the acceptance boundary test to PASS with committed evidence.

topPriorities.title: Harden the tool and evidence execution surfaces that function as policy-enforcement points
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Security intent is weakest where enforcement still depends on sharp procedural execution paths rather than deterministic hardened controls.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Risks, plan, and the adoption plan all keep shell-based execution removal, pinned command/environment assumptions, and security-critical tooling hardening as the next major control-quality step after boundary enforcement.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Remove shell-based evidence/tool execution paths, pin command and environment assumptions, and verify those surfaces as security-critical controls.

topPriorities.title: Close the posture → evidence → enforcement loop for PXS consumption
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Security posture only becomes trustworthy for a consuming environment when baseline claims, evidence, and promotion checks are reproducible and narrow.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Metrics, interfaces, risks, and the deployment baseline all show that reproducible evidence and explicit security-impacting promotion checks are not yet tight enough.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Move baseline-critical references toward committed or reproducible evidence, run one full Security Guardrails VERIFY cycle with recorded evidence, and define the minimum promotion checks for security-impacting PXS changes.

constraints.title: OS↔PXS cross-domain reads are still allowed in acceptance evidence
constraints.impact: Prevents Security from claiming that the declared boundary is a real enforced control and leaves the largest current blast-radius gap open.

constraints.title: Posture-critical evidence is not yet consistently committed/reproducible
constraints.impact: Limits auditability, baseline trustworthiness, and the ability to gate promotions with narrow, replayable security evidence.

risksOrOpportunities.title: OS↔PXS boundary is not yet enforced as a real control
High-risk execution surfaces remain procedural rather than hardened
Posture evidence is not always reproducible from committed artifacts
Artifact-first research layer can make Security learning cumulative and easier to synthesize

researchDelta.summary: Security adopted a broad domain map and radar with three bounded deep-dive themes: OS↔PXS boundary enforcement, tool/evidence execution-surface hardening, and AI-agent runtime/tool-abuse controls.

proposedTdeActions.title: Prioritize closure of the Vega/PXS boundary enforcement fail
proposedTdeActions.why: This remains the clearest highest-risk gap between declared Security architecture and actual enforced runtime behavior.

proposedTdeActions.title: Harden evidence/tool execution paths as explicit security controls
proposedTdeActions.why: The next strongest leverage point is removing procedural shell/path assumptions at policy-enforcement surfaces.

proposedTdeActions.title: Use the new Security research layer to broaden surveillance while keeping only three active deep dives
proposedTdeActions.why: This tests whether artifact-first research improves signal quality without polluting Control Tower context.
